briefings.title: 7 things Bezos, MrBeast & Thiel do that you don’t
briefings.tldr: Sam Parr and Shaan Puri analyze the extreme, frame-breaking management tactics of legendary CEOs—including Bezos, MrBeast, and Thiel—while weighing the personal costs of chasing absolute business greatness against simply being a good person.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sam Parr and Shaan Puri analyze the extreme, frame-breaking management tactics of legendary CEOs—including Bezos, MrBeast, and Thiel—while weighing the personal costs of chasing absolute business greatness against simply being a good person.

## The CEO Hardcore Playbook: Incentives & Operations
*   **Option Drop:** Shared by Martin Basiri (Founder of Applyboard & Passage). 
    *   *Mechanism:* Rather than relying on static company values, Basiri uses instant equity rewards ("option drops") on the spot—awarding 50,000 options for great ideas or impromptu late-night work—to reinforce desired behaviors in real time.
*   **Friction Removal Service:** Used by OpenAI. 
    *   *Mechanism:* To combat bureaucratic bloat as the company scales, employees can email `friction@openai.com` with any administrative drag or roadblock, which a dedicated triage person then systematically investigates and eliminates.

## Communication & Focus Hacks
*   **One-Bit Communication:** Utilized by the Siemens CEO and Jeff Bezos.
    *   *Siemens Approach:* The CEO responds to emails with exclusively "okay" or "no," holding zero recurring calendar meetings; if more detail is needed, employees must talk to him immediately in person.
    *   *Bezos Approach:* Bezos famously forwarded random customer complaints to executives with a single question mark ("?"), signaling the executive team to investigate potential systemic machine failures rather than just addressing isolated anecdotes.
*   **Single-Tasking Enforcement:** Utilized by Peter Thiel at PayPal.
    *   *Mechanism:* Thiel forced extreme focus by physically walking out of the room if employees attempted to bring up any topic outside of their single assigned primary problem.
    *   *The Output Law:* Thiel's philosophy is that "focus is convex"—moving from 80% to 90% focus doesn't just add 10%, it doubles your impact and separates top performers from the rest.

## Resource Culling & Talent Cloning
*   **Continuous Culling:** Utilized by Jack Welch at GE.
    *   *Rules:* Every business division had to be #1 or #2 in its market within one year, or it was fixed, sold, or closed; additionally, Welch fired the bottom 10% of company performers every single year.
*   **Employee Cloning:** Utilized by Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast).
    *   *Mechanism:* In Beast Industries' early days, new key hires shadowed Donaldson from the moment he woke up until he went to sleep for six months straight, turning them into exact mental proxies who knew how he would make every decision.

## The Cost of Greatness vs. "Just Being Great"
*   **The Kevin Kelly Framework:** As discussed via David Perell's interview with Wired co-founder Kevin Kelly, achieving historical greatness requires an extreme, unbalanced life. Kelly consciously surrendered the path of greatness to live a flexible, exploratory life as a "gadfly."
*   **The Mother Teresa & Historical Legacy Reality:** True long-term legacy is rarely bought through money or corporate success; centuries later, people forget billionaires, while remembering inventors, artists, and humanitarians.
*   **The Shift to Daily Character:** Shaan Puri and Sam Parr conclude that instead of chasing abstract, multi-generational corporate greatness (which carries a brutal personal price tag, such as missing out on young children's lives), the better target is "active greatness"—showing up with character, kindness, and excellence in everyday, micro-moments.

## Notable Quotes
> "The more specific, the more concrete, and the more immediate a reward, the more of that behavior you're going to get." 
> — **Sam Parr**

> "To have this life I have, I had to give up on greatness." 
> — **Kevin Kelly** (as shared by Sam Parr)

> "There's a big difference between achieving something great and being great... being great, the active tense, the day-to-day thing, that's the thing to chase." 
> — **Shaan Puri**

briefings.title: Bessent Says China Was 'Dissenter', Blocking Unanimous G20 Communique (Full Remarks)
briefings.tldr: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that China was the sole dissenter blocking a unanimous G20 communique in Asheville, North Carolina, over disagreements on global trade imbalances and non-market export surpluses.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that China was the sole dissenter blocking a unanimous G20 communique in Asheville, North Carolina, over disagreements on global trade imbalances and non-market export surpluses. Meanwhile, Bessent defended the administration's economic strategy, pointing to strong private sector growth, ongoing efforts to economically squeeze Iran, and anticipated productivity-driven disinflation from AI investments.

## G20 Summit & Global Economic Imbalances
* **China as Dissenter:** **Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent** stated that the People's Republic of China was the sole dissenter preventing a unanimous joint communique, citing its world-leading and unsustainable current account surplus.
  * *Coalition Alignment:* 19 other G20 members agreed that non-market-based economies pushing out endless cheap exports represent an unsustainable equilibrium.
  * *Chairman's Statement:* Bessent noted a chairman's statement would be issued reflecting the consensus and key issues of the 19 supporting members.
* **Sovereign Debt & Financial Literacy:** 
  * *Debt Restructuring:* The summit set the stage to make emerging market sovereign debt restructuring faster, more transparent, and more predictable.
  * *Citizen Literacy:* Discussions addressed helping families navigate complex financial choices and sophisticated fraud across G20 nations.
* **Private Sector Integration:** For the first time in G20 history, private sector business leaders joined ministers and central bank governors to discuss practical barriers to investment, innovation, and regulatory confidence.

## Iran Conflict and Economic Sanctions
* **Economic Squeeze on Iran:** **Scott Bessent** described Iran as being in an economic "death spiral" driven by secondary sanctions and Operation Economic Outcast.
  * *Currency Collapse:* The Iranian currency has deteriorated from 800,000 to the dollar 16 months ago to 2.1 million to the dollar.
  * *Energy Constraints:* Iran now faces all-night, 4-hour gas lines despite holding major energy resources.
  * *Financial Network Disruption:* The administration is actively closing RMB conversion channels, cash houses, and banks (such as a Dubai bank shut down on Friday) to starve the regime of funds.
* **Kinetic Actions & Strait of Hormuz:** 
  * *Radar Strikes:* Recent limited kinetic strikes targeted patched-up radar systems along the banks of the Strait of Hormuz.
  * *Media Misinformation:* Bessent criticized media outlets for repeating Iranian "agitprop" regarding mines in the strait, asserting that Iran does not control the waterway.
* **China & International Cooperation:** 
  * *Strait Alignment:* Bessent held quiet conversations with Russia and China, noting China agrees that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open and that Iran cannot possess a nuclear weapon, given that China sources 50% of its energy from the Gulf.

## US Domestic Economy, Inflation, and Energy
* **Growth and Real Wages:** **Scott Bessent** attributed elevated Treasury bond yields to a strong American growth story rather than structural weakness.
  * *Wage Metrics:* Contrasted past Biden administration metrics (a 4% average purchasing power decrease, 21.5% inflation, and 17.5% wage growth) with current real wage gains, particularly for the bottom quartile of earners.
  * *Temporary Pressures:* Energy prices are acknowledged as temporarily elevated but expected to decline.
* **Local & Regional Impact (North Carolina):** 
  * *Tourism Boost:* The Asheville G20 event is estimated to generate more than $20 million in local benefits, with delegates planning extended stays.
  * *Manufacturing Reshoring:* Highlighted industrial investments, such as John Deere building a new factory and reshoring operations in North Carolina.
* **Tax Reform & The Laffer Connection:** Acknowledged Dr. Arthur Laffer as a Reagan-era pioneer and mentor who helped craft full expensing rules for equipment, factories, and agricultural structures, fueling an industrial construction boom.

## Artificial Intelligence & Infrastructure Buildout
* **Global AI Strategy & Guardrails:** 
  * *Superpower Dominance:* **Scott Bessent** stated the US currently holds 50% of global compute and is projected to reach **80% of global compute by 2028**.
  * *Bilateral Talks:* AI guardrails and communication were briefly discussed at the G20 and are expected to be on the agenda when President Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Washington in September.
* **Productivity and Economic Impact:** 
  * *CapEx to Productivity:* Bessent compared current AI capital expenditures to an Alan Greenspan "conundrum," predicting that massive CapEx will soon translate into highly disinflationary productivity gains.
  * *Startup Boom:* Data indicates AI is fueling a massive increase in small-business startups, enabling 1- to 3-person companies to achieve critical mass.
* **Public Relations and Misinformation:** 
  * *Communications Failure:* Bessent argued that AI labs and data center builders have done a "horrendous job" explaining themselves and must reset public trust to ensure benefits do not accrue to a small group.
  * *Foreign Interference:* Bessent asserted that a large number of local sites pushing back against AI infrastructure buildouts are foreign-backed, specifically citing Chinese "adverse propaganda."

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **AI Productivity Timeline:** "I would guess that in the next 6 months, we will start seeing the benefits of that [CapEx turning into productivity]." — Scott Bessent
* **Global Compute Share Target:** "By 2028, we will be at 80% of global compute [up from 50% today]." — Scott Bessent

## Notable Quotes
> *"It is clear that the country with the world's largest and unsustainable current account surplus, People's Republic of China, was the dissenter."* — Scott Bessent
> 
> *"The G20 is at its best when it does what it was created to do: identify the world's leading economies together to confront difficult questions, identify where our interests converge and then turn that agreement into action."* — Scott Bessent
> 
> *"The media immediately publishes all the lies... This is Iranian agitprop and everyone in this audience and every news outlet should be ashamed for publishing that, taking a lying regime at face value."* — Scott Bessent
> 
> *"How did you go bankrupt? Slowly then quickly. Well, I think we're in the acceleration phase."* — Scott Bessent

briefings.title: Commerce Sec. Lutnick and Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown speak at G20 meeting — 9/2/2026
briefings.tldr: AI capabilities and demand are scaling exponentially, driven by systematic compute and data scaling laws that require an unprecedented global industrial buildout of data centers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI capabilities and demand are scaling exponentially, driven by systematic compute and data scaling laws that require an unprecedented global industrial buildout of data centers. Anthropic Co-Founder Tom Brown and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick discussed how global infrastructure investments and autonomous AI collaborators can radically accelerate human prosperity and scientific innovation.

## AI Scaling, Economic Growth, and Cost Trends
* **Exponential Demand and Infrastructure:** AI capabilities and demand are growing in multiples every year, triggering the largest industrial buildout in human history, surpassing the scale of 1800s railroads.
* **Scaling Laws and Predictability:** In 2019, Anthropic co-founders published a scaling laws paper establishing a scientific recipe relating compute, data, and model size to intelligence levels across 15 orders of magnitude.
* **Economic Doubling and Cost Reductions:** The economic value generated across frontier AI labs is quadrupling every year (doubling every 6 months), while the cost to access a model equivalent to the previous year's smartest model drops by roughly 20x annually.
* **Internal Operations:** The majority of intellectual labor at Anthropic is now performed autonomously by models operating with the same permissions and tool access as human co-workers.

## Global Infrastructure and G20 Participation
* **Data Center Bottlenecks:** The primary bottleneck to progress is a shortage of power and labor required to build sufficient data centers globally.
* **Ratepayer and Grid Pledges:** Major AI labs have signed ratepayer pledges to bring new power generation on behind the meter and return excess capacity to the grid.
* **The "Red Carpet" Requirement:** Secretary Lutnick emphasized that nations must roll out the red carpet to attract data center investment rather than creating regulatory friction.
* **Prerequisites for Expansion:** Building data centers requires government-level support for land permitting and construction labor, which in turn generates high-value jobs and tax revenue.

## Applications in Science and Intellectual Labor
* **Focus on Coding and Complex Tasks:** Anthropic intentionally focused on coding and intellectual labor because software engineering can be performed entirely within computers without physical laboratory experiments.
* **Mathematical and Scientific Breakthroughs:** Frontier models have advanced from undergraduate-level math proficiency over the last three months to ranking among the top 100 mathematicians in specific subfields.
* **Solving Major Medical Challenges:** Scale-up of AI models aims to overcome the bottleneck of scarce human researchers to accelerate breakthroughs against diseases like cancer by orders of magnitude.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Tom Brown:** AI model capabilities will continue increasing at roughly the same rate from an intelligence perspective over the coming years.
* **Tom Brown:** Within the next 12 months, frontier AI models will achieve the level of "once-in-a-generation" scientists capable of making massive breakthroughs in key scientific fields.

## Notable Quotes
> "The things that makes us special is our minds. It's not our body. The industrial revolution transformed all of society. But really, it was like the second most important thing about humans is our bodies. The main thing is our is our minds."
> — Tom Brown

> "Often people are not ambitious enough in what they ask the models to do... the way that I see the best people who get the most value out of the models using them now is instead they treat them like they would treat a collaborator like a co-worker in their organization."
> — Tom Brown

briefings.title: Commerce Sec. Lutnick and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a fireside chat at G20 meeting — 9/2/2026
briefings.tldr: Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick discussed AI as the greatest platform shift in human history, framing it as physical economic infrastructure that manufactures digital intelligence (measured in tokens) akin to electricity.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick discussed AI as the greatest platform shift in human history, framing it as physical economic infrastructure that manufactures digital intelligence (measured in tokens) akin to electricity. They urged G20 leaders to invest in local AI infrastructure to avoid being left behind while balancing safety regulations with a growth-driven mindset.

## AI as Economic Infrastructure and the Token Economy
* **The Token Economy:** **Jensen Huang** explained that AI computes "tokens" as a mathematical outcome representing intelligence, functioning identically to energy monetization ($ per kilowatt-hour vs. $ per million tokens).
* **Democratization of Intelligence:** **Jensen Huang** noted that AI is the great equalizer, allowing anyone in the world to program a computer using human language rather than restricted traditional programming.
* **The Five-Layer Cake of AI:** **Jensen Huang** broke down the technology stack:
    * Layer 1: Energy (transforms electricity into mathematics)
    * Layer 2: Chips (Nvidia's GPU hardware layer)
    * Layer 3: Infrastructure (large data centers, land, power, shells)
    * Layer 4: AI models (language, biology, chemistry, physics, robotics)
    * Layer 5: Data and applications (the most vital layer for national benefit)

## National Investment and Global Strategy
* **Infrastructure Imperative:** **Howard Lutnick** and **Jensen Huang** emphasized that every G20 country must build local data centers and digital intellectual capacity to support researchers, students, and startups.
* **Sovereign Intelligence:** **Jensen Huang** advised nations not to outsource all intelligence to external parties, stressing that local infrastructure acts as a catalyst for domestic innovation.
* **U.S. Manufacturing and Energy Reindustrialization:** **Howard Lutnick** and **Jensen Huang** highlighted that the U.S. pro-energy growth agenda is channeling nearly $1 trillion into domestic infrastructure in 2026, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs across chip fabs, computer plants, and AI factories while modernizing the energy grid.

## Hardware, Robotics, and Architecture
* **Embodied AI:** **Jensen Huang** explained that large language models combined with "agent harnesses" transition into physical robotics, self-driving cars, surgical robots, and autonomous drug discovery labs.
* **Fungible and Durable Compute:** **Jensen Huang** stated that Nvidia's 14th-generation GPU architecture is general-purpose and fungible—supporting every closed/open model and modality—making it a safe, durable investment for costly infrastructures where 1 gigawatt costs $50B–$60B.

## Societal Impact, Regulation, and the Future of Work
* **Balancing Safety and Growth:** **Jensen Huang** argued that the single worst outcome for any country is being left behind due to fear-driven messaging, comparing AI adoption to the airline and auto industries where safety is an engineering responsibility rather than a user burden.
* **Pragmatic Regulation:** **Jensen Huang** urged regulators to avoid legislating hypothetical harms and instead focus on actual, pragmatic harms while allowing the technology's S-curve to advance and self-correct.
* **Supercharged Ambition, Not Job Loss:** **Jensen Huang** dismissed the idea that AI will eliminate all jobs, explaining that human roles are defined by purpose and context, and that workers will be "supercharged" to tackle $100 trillion industries.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **AGI Timeline:** "In the next couple of years, we are going to achieve essentially what people call AGI. And and that's not an illogical thing to me. In fact, I would argue that we're practically there today." — Jensen Huang
* **Infrastructure Buildout Scale:** "Between now and the end of the decade 100 gigawatts [will be built] because we want to produce intelligence for the world." — Jensen Huang
* **U.S. Infrastructure Investment:** "This year alone we're going to invest close to a trillion dollars into the world's into the United States infrastructure." — Jensen Huang
* **Accelerated Timelines:** "Things that take 10 years are going to take one. Things that take one will take a month." — Jensen Huang

## Notable Quotes
> "This is the first time in history that all of us have been using computer tech computer technology, where you're not buying a device, but we're producing economic infrastructure." 
> — Jensen Huang

> "The worst outcome is that you don't take advantage of it. That you are left behind. That is the single worst outcome." 
> — Jensen Huang

> "You can't outsource all of your intelligence to somebody else. And so, you have to use as much of it as you can, build as much as you need to." 
> — Jensen Huang

briefings.title: Commerce Sec. Lutnick and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman participate in a fireside chat — 9/2/2026
briefings.tldr: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick discussed the trajectory of artificial intelligence at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, framing AI as a transformative economic engine comparable to electricity or the industrial revolution.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick discussed the trajectory of artificial intelligence at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, framing AI as a transformative economic engine comparable to electricity or the industrial revolution. Altman emphasized that AI represents a massive democratization of intelligence and entrepreneurship, while stressing the critical need to make the technology globally abundant and safe.

## Evolution and Timeline of OpenAI
- **Origins and Early Years:** 
  - Founded in late 2015, with the first day of work in January 2016.
  - Initial focus was on reinforcement learning tasks (e.g., training a robot hand to solve a Rubik's Cube, playing video games) rather than language models.
- **Milestones in Model Development:**
  - **2018:** Progress began on unsupervised learning and the first GPT-1 model.
  - **2020:** GPT-3 trained, serving as the first model to cross a threshold of usability (generating coherent sentences).
  - **March 2023:** GPT-4 launched (after 8 months of internal testing), marking the consensus moment where internal skeptics realized the technology's immense potential.
- **Current and Upcoming Releases:** 
  - Sam Altman noted that OpenAI is launching a new model soon, representing another major step forward in doing science, creating complex software, and adding economic value.

## Economic Impact and Entrepreneurship
- **Boom in Small Businesses:** 
  - AI acts as an unprecedented catalyst for entrepreneurship, allowing individuals without large capital or expert teams to manage supply chains, write legal contracts, and handle marketing.
  - Altman cited an early 2023 example of a laundromat manager using ChatGPT to run a struggling business.
- **Workforce Evolution:** 
  - The evolution moved from early text generation to coding agents and white-collar work agents in 2025.
  - Altman predicts a third wave featuring long-term persistent agents acting as constant virtual collaborators.
  - **Productivity Acceleration:** Work that took 3 months at a startup accelerator can now be accomplished in roughly 17 minutes using tools like Codex.
- **National Strategy:** 
  - Altman asserted that integrating AI is non-negotiable for G20 economies; whether countries build or rent data centers, ignoring AI means missing out on vital economic growth and individual quality of life.

## OpenAI's Philosophy and Differentiation
- **The Pragmatist Approach:** 
  - OpenAI aims to avoid the traps of both blind optimism and doomerism, focusing on realistic navigation of transformation and risk.
- **Platform and Sovereignty:** 
  - Positioned as a reliable platform and service provider that respects national sovereignty, allowing different countries to apply AI according to their own rules.
- **Anti-Monopoly and Pro-Human Stance:** 
  - OpenAI explicitly desires the global economy to succeed without sucking up all the value or acting as the sole company.
  - Altman emphasized that OpenAI is firmly and proudly on "team humanity," ensuring people remain at the center of the economy, society, and global decision-making.

## Infrastructure, Efficiency, and Risks
- **The Scale of Compute Demand:** 
  - Token usage has exploded: an OpenAI employee was the world token leader at ~100,000 tokens/month in early 2020, whereas top users in mid-2026 reach hundreds of billions of tokens/month, with global per capita usage also scaling dramatically.
  - Altman projected that per-capita token usage will scale up to 100 billion tokens/month, and top users will consume 100 quadrillion tokens/month over the next 6.5 years.
- **Abundance vs. Inequality:** 
  - To prevent AI from becoming a scarce, highly priced commodity hoarded by the rich, massive infrastructure investments and efficiency gains (algorithmic and hardware) are required to make intelligence abundant and inexpensive.
- **Managing Critical Risks:** 
  - **Cybersecurity:** Altman warned that cybersecurity is a top-and-center risk where things could go very wrong unless acted upon urgently.
  - **Biosecurity:** Acknowledged as another major challenge in the next 5 years that must be successfully navigated alongside the risk of power concentration and lack of abundance.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Token Usage Scale:** Sam Altman projects that within 6.5 years, the average per capita use of tokens will reach 100 billion tokens per month, and peak individual usage will reach 100 quadrillion tokens per month.
- **Everyday Integration:** Altman predicts that a decade from now, people will no longer talk about AI because it will be universally embedded in every product and service, much like electricity today.

## Notable Quotes
> "If I were a country, ... for sure, I think it is non-negotiable that you have to use it. The economic growth and benefit to people that can come from this, the value to a country is too high to ignore."
> — Sam Altman

> "We are very firmly and very proudly on team humanity; we would like to build tools for people... and that people should run the future, not AI."
> — Sam Altman

> "The work that we expected a startup to accomplish in 3 months is now probably doable in like 17 minutes with Codex."
> — Sam Altman

briefings.title: Commerce Sec. Lutnick and Palantir CEO Alex Karp participate in a fireside chat — 9/2/2026
briefings.tldr: Alex Karp (Palantir CEO) and Howard Lutnick (Commerce Secretary) discussed AI sovereignty and ecosystem strategy at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, emphasizing that nations must secure their own data and technical stacks rather than inadvertently exporting proprietary intelligence to American frontier labs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
**Alex Karp (Palantir CEO)** and **Howard Lutnick (Commerce Secretary)** discussed AI sovereignty and ecosystem strategy at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, emphasizing that nations must secure their own data and technical stacks rather than inadvertently exporting proprietary intelligence to American frontier labs.

## The AI Technology Stack & Sovereignty

* **Sovereignty Requirements:** **Alex Karp** outlined the essential layers a nation must control to avoid technological dependency:
  * **Compute & Power:** Nations need access to compute infrastructure and abundant electricity, noting France's nuclear strategy as a positive model for power generation.
  * **Data Control:** Every nation must ensure its proprietary data (e.g., nuclear reactor specifications, internal security parameters) remains within its own secure perimeter.
  * **Application & Integration Layer:** Positioned north and south of the AI models, Palantir's ontology acts as an integration layer enabling countries to train and control models without data exfiltration.
* **The Danger of Uncontrolled LLM Deployment:** **Alex Karp** sharply criticized current regulatory frameworks outside America, stating that deploying large language models without technical oversight leads companies to unintentionally exfiltrate proprietary alpha and national secrets to frontier model providers.

## Open vs. Frontier Models & Indigenous Ecosystems

* **Model Strategy and Customization:** **Alex Karp** explained that nations will rely on a mix of frontier and non-frontier (open-source) models:
  * Open models can outperform frontier models on specific, localized vectors when fine-tuned on precise questions within a closed environment.
  * Countries can leverage weaker indigenous models (citing a hypothetical example from Chile) alongside more powerful architectures, maintaining control over both.
* **Avoiding Western vs. Indigenous Dependence:** **Alex Karp** noted that Palantir helps foreign clients build "Plan B" architectures so they are not entirely dependent on the Palantir stack or American infrastructure, particularly in sensitive defense and battlefield contexts.

## Regulation, Technical Expertise, and Geopolitics

* **The Technical Expertise Gap in Regulation:** **Alex Karp** warned that non-technical regulators often rely on advice from entities with commercial interests in selling technology, leading to policies that undermine national sovereignty.
* **Reclaiming National Technical Talent:** **Alex Karp** urged G20 nation leaders to bring home domestic technical titans working abroad, placing them directly into policymaking roles alongside government leaders to dictate regulatory standards, chip procurement, and software stack choices.
* **Global Advantages in Production vs. Adoption:** **Alex Karp** contrasted geopolitical regions:
  * **United States:** Holds an enormous advantage in the production and dissemination of AI technology.
  * **Japan, Korea, China, and Middle Eastern Arab Nations:** Benefit from distinct political structures or societal orders that face fewer domestic friction points regarding AI adoption and wealth distribution compared to Western democracies.
  * **Europe:** Faces an extreme disadvantage in AI adoption due to over-regulation and political friction, though European civil liberties traditions (such as data purging mandates) differ fundamentally from American approaches.

## Notable Quotes

> "Whoever's telling you this works needs to be fired because they are hurting your country. They're not hurting me, but this is literally the way to export every one of your secrets to some other company. And it's only because the people doing the regulation don't actually understand the technical material."  
> — **Alex Karp**

> "I don't want to hear how much money you're going to spend. Who's going to get the money? Like the money doesn't matter as much as who gets it. And that is crucial."  
> — **Alex Karp**

> "Under the condition that everyone goes home and says, 'Okay, we didn't really take this seriously'... and saying this is game time. How serious are we? And and I do think you should get access to all the classified data... Then I'm very optimistic."  
> — **Alex Karp**

briefings.title: FULL INTERVIEW: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Speaks With Howard Lutnick At G20 Ministerial | AI1F
briefings.tldr: AI is a five-layer stack—from energy to data and applications—that democratizes computing and requires every country and enterprise to build local digital infrastructure to capture economic growth.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
AI is a five-layer stack—from energy to data and applications—that democratizes computing and requires every country and enterprise to build local digital infrastructure to capture economic growth. Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang and U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick emphasize that while AGI is nearly here, AI automates tasks rather than eliminating jobs, supercharging human ambition and productivity across a multi-trillion-dollar technological revolution.

## The Five-Layer AI Stack and Sovereign Infrastructure
* **The Five-Layer Architecture:** Jensen Huang breaks down artificial intelligence into a structured stack:
  * **Layer 1 (Energy):** Transforms electricity into mathematics.
  * **Layer 2 (Chips):** The GPU hardware tier led by Nvidia.
  * **Layer 3 (Infrastructure):** Large data centers incorporating land, power, and shell architecture.
  * **Layer 4 (AI Models):** Models spanning languages, biology, chemicals, physics, and robotics.
  * **Layer 5 (Data and Applications):** The most critical layer where actual value and user interaction occur.
* **Sovereign Infrastructure Investment:** Howard Lutnick and Jensen Huang emphasize that every country must build local digital infrastructure to support researchers, students, startups, and industries.
  * **Local Activation:** Deploying local infrastructure immediately activates domestic startup ecosystems and academic research.
  * **Fungible and Durable Hardware:** Nvidia operates on its 14th architectural generation, providing general-purpose GPUs that run every closed, open, physical, and biological model across clouds, on-premise setups, and edge devices.
  * **Capital Scaling:** Infrastructure buildouts are capital-intensive, with a single gigawatt costing approximately $50 billion to $60 billion.

## Democratization of Intelligence and Workforce Impact
* **Democratization via Human Language:** Anyone can now program a computer using natural human language, elevating everyone as a universal equalizer.
* **Agentic Systems:** AI has evolved from static large language models (LLMs) into "agentic systems" surrounded by digital exoskeletons that retrieve knowledge, maintain working memory, use digital tools, and operate physical machinery.
* **Physical AI Integration:** Agentic systems are deployed into physical machinery, including self-driving cars, manufacturing robotic arms, logistics vehicles, surgical robots, and autonomous drug discovery laboratories.
* **Job Evolution over Elimination:** Jensen Huang rejects the notion that AI will eliminate jobs, comparing onboarding an AI agent to onboarding a PhD graduate from MIT, Stanford, or Harvard:
  * **Context and Purpose:** Companies must surround AI agents with context, purpose, relevance, and environmental harnessing.
  * **Task vs. Job:** Routine typing and talking tasks are automated, but human jobs—defined by purpose and meaning—remain intact while supercharging overall productivity.

## Regulatory Balance and Economic Growth
* **Pragmatic Regulation:** Regulation must target actual, pragmatic harm rather than hypothetical, theoretical risks, allowing fast innovation along the S-curve to inherently improve safety.
* **Avoiding Fear-Driven Stagnation:** The worst outcome for any country is failing to adopt AI due to fear, uncertainty, and excessive focus on risk rather than prosperity and opportunity.
* **Economic Scale and Job Creation:** 
  * **U.S. Infrastructure Spending:** The United States is investing close to $1 trillion into domestic infrastructure this year, generating hundreds of thousands of jobs across chip fabs, computer plants, and AI factories.
  * **Macro Ambition:** Innovations target a $100 trillion global industry, unlocking an estimated $20 trillion to $50 trillion in new economic benefit worldwide.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **AGI Timeline:** "In the next couple of years, we are going to achieve essentially what people call AGI. And... we're practically there today." — Jensen Huang
* **Infrastructure Scaling Target:** "Between now and the end of the decade [we are] building 100 gigawatts because we want to produce intelligence for the world." — Jensen Huang
* **Investment Velocity:** "This year alone we're going to invest close to a trillion dollars into the world's into the United States infrastructure and that's generating enormous economic growth..." — Jensen Huang

---

## Notable Quotes
> "The first thing is to recognize what is AI... AI is, if I could simply, a five layer cake. At the lowest layer is energy... And the most important part of AI is the fifth layer, the layer above that which is data and applications."
> — Jensen Huang

> "The worst outcome is that you don't take advantage of it. That you are left behind. That is the single worst outcome. And that outcome comes from... talking about the technology with fear with uncertainty."
> — Jensen Huang

> "For the first time, you're hearing innovators, people, companies, countries talking about elevating a hundred trillion dollar industry. That's ambition."
> — Jensen Huang

briefings.title: How Thomson Reuters Achieved ‘Fiduciary-Grade’ AI Accuracy
briefings.tldr: Thomson Reuters President and CEO Steve Hasker outlines how the company leverages "fiduciary-grade AI" and proprietary data to drive growth across the legal, tax, and news sectors without sacrificing accuracy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Thomson Reuters President and CEO Steve Hasker outlines how the company leverages "fiduciary-grade AI" and proprietary data to drive growth across the legal, tax, and news sectors without sacrificing accuracy. He also addresses token cost management, internal employee adoption, and strategic restructuring.

## Thomson Reuters: Business Overview & Growth Drivers
* **Company Profile (2026 Overview):** Described by **Steve Hasker** as the largest provider of content and technology to the legal profession, the largest provider of tax calculation engines, a major risk/fraud/compliance business, and the owner of Reuters News (the world's largest wholesaler of news, representing about 10% of the overall business).
* **Core Growth Drivers:** 
  * **Coping with Complexity:** Providing content-driven technology that enables decision-makers to comply with growing legal and regulatory complexity without adding headcount.
  * **AI Product Expansion:** Moving from traditional search (like *Westlaw*) into work-product generation (first drafts of contracts, briefs, motions) and automating activities around tax return preparation.

## "Fiduciary-Grade" AI vs. Consumer AI
* **Definition of Fiduciary-Grade:** **Steve Hasker** coined this term for AI used by professionals (lawyers, tax, accounting, audit) who cannot afford hallucinations or incorrect citations due to risks to their professional licenses and client relationships. Outputs must be deterministic, not probabilistic.
* **Four Pillars of Accuracy:**
  * **Proprietary Content:** Decades- and centuries-old data sets (*Westlaw*, *Practical Law*, *Checkpoint*, *CLEAR*) maintained by thousands of experts.
  * **On-Site Domain Experts:** A couple of thousand reference attorneys and CPAs who produce content and train AI agents to behave like tenured professionals.
  * **Data Privacy Guarantees:** A strict promise that customer inputs will not become part of the AI output.
  * **Human Support Infrastructure:** Dedicated call centers where users can trace and walk through the exact logic, output, and citations of an AI query.
* **The Thompson Model:** **Steve Hasker** highlights the launch of *Thomson Model*, a large language model built specifically for legal (and expanding to tax/accounting/audit) that outperforms cutting-edge frontier models on specific professional tasks.

## Token Costs, Budgets, and the Customer ROI Gap
* **Managing Token Costs:** **Steve Hasker** acknowledges that token costs for frontier models have risen exponentially. Thomson Reuters covers these within Wall Street guidance, but the *Thomson Model* provides internal financial flexibility should external token costs become unmanageable.
* **The Customer ROI Lag:** 
  * While 74% of professionals use AI weekly, 91% feel organizations fall short on translating this into value, and 33% of legal/accounting professionals turn to unsanctioned tools creating unmanaged risks.
  * **Steve Hasker** notes an 18-to-24-month lag for firms to rewire workflows, prompting Thomson Reuters to deploy forward-deployed engineers and customer success consultants to drive change management.

## Human Capital and Newsroom Transformation
* **Engineering Retooling:** Clarified that recent engineering adjustments (such as 500 job reductions mentioned in reports) are a retooling for agentic AI talent rather than cost-cutting efficiencies.
* **Workforce AI Adoption:** Encouraging 27,000 employees to automate mundane, repetitive tasks. 
* **Reuters Newsroom Impact:** **Steve Hasker** projects that Reuters' news output will increase three-to-four-fold over the next few years with roughly the same headcount (around 2,700 journalists across 200 locations), driven by AI assisting long-term partners like the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG).

## Strategic Transactions and Leadership Lessons
* **Global Print Joint Venture:** **Steve Hasker** discussed a transaction with KKR giving them a 51% stake in the 140-year-old global print business for $500 million in gross proceeds, allowing Thomson Reuters to focus entirely on its digital and AI business.
* **Daily Customer Engagement:** **Steve Hasker** maintains a commitment to speaking with a Thomson Reuters customer *every single day* to understand industry challenges and maintain effectiveness.
* **Career Philosophy:** Reflecting on his career across PwC (Melbourne), McKinsey (11 years), Nielsen, and CIA Global, **Steve Hasker** emphasizes that he never had a career plan, instead following a "North Star" of prioritizing continuous learning.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Workflow Rewiring Timeline:** Firms will take **18 months to two years** to truly rewire workflows and realize the ROI on AI tools — *Steve Hasker*.
* **Newsroom Output Growth:** Reuters news output will increase **three-to-four-fold over the next few years** with approximately the same or slightly higher headcount — *Steve Hasker*.
* **One-Year Target:** In 12 months, Thomson Reuters expects to report **double-digit growth within its core "big three" business** and demonstrate positive, measurable ROI (such as partner profit increases and efficiency step-ups) for customers using agentic AI — *Steve Hasker*.

## Notable Quotes
> "Fiduciary-grade AI is that additional higher standard where the results need to be deterministic not probabilistic."
> — Steve Hasker

> "AI will not take your job, but someone using AI may take your job."
> — Steve Hasker

briefings.title: Inside Moderna’s Biggest mRNA Test Since COVID
briefings.tldr: Moderna and Merck achieved positive Phase 3 results for their individualized mRNA cancer treatment (mRNA-4157/V940) combined with Keytruda in melanoma, marking the first time a personalized cancer vaccine has met its primary endpoint across a major clinical trial.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Moderna and Merck achieved positive Phase 3 results for their individualized mRNA cancer treatment (mRNA-4157/V940) combined with Keytruda in melanoma, marking the first time a personalized cancer vaccine has met its primary endpoint across a major clinical trial.

## Clinical Trial Results & Phase 3 Milestones
* **Primary Endpoint Success:** Stéphane Bancel (CEO, Moderna) noted that the Phase 3 clinical trial in melanoma met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS), significantly reducing cancer return or death compared to Keytruda alone.
* **Secondary Endpoint Achievement:** The trial also met its secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) during the first interim analysis, which was an unexpected and positive surprise given that it requires more time to mature.
* **Phase 2 Long-Term Durability:** At ASCO in spring 2026, Moderna showed that Phase 2 data at five years post-treatment demonstrated an ~50% recurrence-free survival advantage for combination therapy vs. Keytruda alone, with ~80% of patients remaining disease-free at five years (considered a clinical cure in oncology).

## Mechanism of Action: mRNA vs. Traditional Checkpoint Inhibitors
* **Complementary Mechanisms:** Stéphane Bancel explained that Keytruda (a checkpoint inhibitor) acts like "opening the gates to let the dogs out" of the immune system, but only works for about 60% of patients while carrying severe autoimmune side effects (e.g., type 1 diabetes, lupus, Crohn's disease).
* **Targeted T-Cell Training:** Rather than unleashing the immune system blindly, Moderna's mRNA treatment encodes the patient's specific tumor mutations so that T-cells are taught at a molecular level exactly which signature to recognize and attack.
* **Intracellular Presentation:** Injected intramuscularly, Moderna's mRNA travels to lymph nodes and enters Antigen-Presenting Cells (APCs), translating the message from within, differing from older protein/peptide vaccines that circulate openly in the blood.

## Personalization & Manufacturing Scale
* **High Individualization Rate:** Roughly 90% of neoantigens identified across patients are completely unique, proving that personalized, end-to-end individualized manufacturing is essential.
* **The 42-Day Process:** From the initial tumor biopsy to the final vaccine ready at the hospital, the needle-to-needle turnaround time is currently roughly 42 days.
* **Manufacturing Engineering & Footprint:** Stéphane Bancel highlighted that manufacturing is fully synthetic and enzymatic (taking place in liquid/water with tiny reactors), allowing for a much smaller clean-room footprint compared to CAR-T cell therapy's large bioreactor volumes. The Marboro, Massachusetts facility is currently capable of producing tens of thousands of doses.

## Expansion Vectors Beyond Melanoma
* **PD-1 Combo Studies:** Moderna and Merck are actively running Phase 3 trials in lung cancer and Phase 2 trials in kidney and bladder cancers where Keytruda is already standard of care.
* **Early-Stage Monotherapy:** Moderna announced a Phase 3 study in spring 2026 for stage 1 lung cancer patients using the mRNA therapy as a monotherapy without checkpoint inhibitors, targeting former smokers screened via X-ray.
* **Cold Tumors:** Trials are underway in notoriously difficult, checkpoint-resistant cancers like pancreatic and gastric cancers, with potential future combinations with targeted therapies like Revolution Medicines' KRAS inhibitors.
* **Platform Horizons:** Stéphane Bancel shared that Moderna is preparing pivotal late-stage data for rare liver genetic diseases in children and is directing its mRNA platform toward treating the root causes of autoimmune diseases.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Stéphane Bancel** predicts that Moderna will file with regulators so the melanoma treatment can be available to patients as soon as possible, with a target of **2027**.
* **Stéphane Bancel** states that the current version of Moderna's individualized cancer mRNA technology (version 1.0) is "the worst version of inisurana you're going to see for the rest of medical history," anticipating algorithmic and technological improvements from mining Phase 3 patient data.
* **Stéphane Bancel** claims that before the end of the year (**2026**), Moderna will have pivotal late-stage study data for rare genetic liver diseases in children.

## Notable Quotes
> *"It's a first of many. It's a first time that there is an agent in melanoma that is better than Keytruda alone... it's the first time there is a cancer vaccine working."*
> — **Stéphane Bancel**

> *"We always joke that the current version of AI is the worst we're going to see in our lifetime. Well, it's exactly the same for Inisurana [mRNA cancer vaccine], which is the current version... is the worst version you're going to see for the rest of medical history."*
> — **Stéphane Bancel**

briefings.title: John Deere CEO: Autonomous Tractors and Farming's AI Era | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: John Deere CEO John May discusses transforming a 190-year-old tractor manufacturer into an AI and precision-technology company, highlighting autonomous farming by 2030 and significant input savings for farmers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** John Deere CEO John May discusses transforming a 190-year-old tractor manufacturer into an AI and precision-technology company, highlighting autonomous farming by 2030 and significant input savings for farmers.

## Smart Industrial Strategy & Customer Focus
- **Customer-Centric Reorganization:** John May explained that John Deere shifted away from building the best standalone machinery (like planters) to focusing entirely on the customer’s production systems and overall profitability.
  - Realigned the corporate structure around crop production teams (corn, soybean, wheat, cotton, sugar) rather than traditional product lines or geographic regions.
  - Delayered the company from 11 corporate layers down to 7 to accelerate decision-making speed.
- **Precision Inputs & Sustainability:** By utilizing AI and computer vision adapted from autonomous driving technology, John Deere machinery drastically reduces waste.
  - **Herbicide Reduction:** Computer vision allows sprayers to differentiate between a weed and a healthy crop, spraying only the weed and cutting herbicide application by **60%**.
  - **Nitrogen Savings:** Instead of free-flowing nitrogen into a trench, computer vision targets the exact seed location during planting, saving **2/3** of the nitrogen cost.

## Autonomous Farming & Technology Integration
- **Autonomous Equipment Rollout:** 
  - Launched a commercial fully autonomous tillage solution in 2023.
  - The portable technology stack works across tractors, combines, and sprayers, allowing equipment to run 24 hours a day without an operator in the cab.
- **Precision Planted Infrastructure:** Modern planters have replaced hydraulics with electric motors, allowing independent row control and micro-adjustments based on soil fertility (e.g., planting 30,000 seeds in one row and 24,000 in another).
- **Redefining the Farmer's Role:** May emphasized that autonomy moves farmers out of the cab to focus on higher-value tasks like planning, monitoring multiple machines, and optimizing system performance.

## Data, Subscriptions, and Business Model Evolution
- **Subscription & Pay-As-You-Go Models:** John Deere introduced Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) and pay-by-the-acre options to help farmers who cannot afford full capital equipment purchases access the latest technology. Take rates have doubled year-over-year.
- **The Operations Center Ecosystem:** Since putting telematics gateways on machines in 2012, John Deere has amassed 15 years of data across 1 million connected machines. 
  - The cloud-based Operations Center houses machine and agronomic data.
  - Farmers can securely share data with third-party input providers (such as Syngenta) to generate customized planting prescriptions sent directly to their machinery.

## Market Conditions and the Farm Income Cycle
- **Global Trade & Supply Disruptions:** Farm income is currently down due to a global convergence of trade flow disruptions, market exits (such as Russia and Ukraine), and geopolitical conflicts (such as the war in Iran affecting fuel and fertilizer costs).
- **Managing Inventory:** To navigate the downturn, John Deere has intentionally underproduced retail demand to stabilize used equipment inventories globally.

## Leadership Philosophy and Background
- **Rooted Beginnings:** May grew up in Caribou, Maine—where the local school system shut down four weeks a year for potato harvesting—and attended college using federal Pell Grants.
- **Corporate Culture:** Stresses a foundational philosophy of putting the customer first and ensuring employees treat everyone with integrity and humanity.
- **Evolution at Deere:** A 30+ year veteran of the company who previously ran operations in China (2004–2007) and took over as CEO in 2019.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- John May stated John Deere’s ambition to make US corn production fully autonomous (tillage, planting, spraying, and harvesting without operator engagement) by **2030**.
- John May predicted that **2026** will mark the bottom of the current farm income and equipment-purchasing cycle, after which the industry will cycle back to a normal market.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you can't manage those weeds, they take the valuable nutrients away from the healthy plant and the healthy plant produces less. So we invested heavily in a technology that was not used in agriculture—computer vision... That reduced herbicide application by 60%."
> — John May

> "Our goal is—our our ambition period is by 2030, we want to have the corn production system, growing corn in the US fully autonomous. That's our goal. Everything from tillage, planting, spraying, and harvesting the crop, without an operator engaging at all."
> — John May

> "You have to have this incredible passion to serve that customer and get better every single day... If the customer is not ringing the cash register, then you don't exist."
> — John May

briefings.title: LIVE: Commerce Sec. Howard Lutnick holds news conference at the G20 Innovation Ministerial — 9/2/26
briefings.tldr: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnik and OSTP Director Michael Kratsios announced a unanimous G20 consensus on the Carolina principles for emerging technology during a press conference in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, emphasizing heavy private sector AI infrastructure investments and the global reach of the American AI stack.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnik and OSTP Director Michael Kratsios announced a unanimous G20 consensus on the Carolina principles for emerging technology during a press conference in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, emphasizing heavy private sector AI infrastructure investments and the global reach of the American AI stack.

## G20 Innovation Ministerial & Consensus
* **Consensus Achievement:** All 20 G20 nations agreed on the G20 innovation ministerial statement after extensive staff-level negotiations.
* **Carolina Principles:** The agreed principles for emerging technology call for governments to:
  * Invest in foundational research to accelerate discovery.
  * Strengthen development and commercialization pathways.
  * Drive trusted adoption and deployment by applying existing sector-specific rules and reserving new regulations strictly for novel considerations.
* **Featured Speakers & Interventions:** Day-one and day-two discussions included contributions from SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, PCAST Co-Chair David Sachs, Commonwealth Fusion Systems CEO Bob Mumgard, Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg, ASU President Michael Crowe, Nobel laureate and Google DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic Co-Founder Tom Brown, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

## Domestic Investments & Economic Development
* **Federal Grants:** The Trump administration awarded $41 million plus an additional $145 million in economic development grants to North Carolina.
* **Private Sector Co-Investment:** Government grants require private sector buy-in, generating a total of **$2.2 billion** in additional private investment and creating over **3,600 jobs** in North Carolina.
* **Industrial AI & Tech Commitments:** Secretary Lutnik highlighted multi-billion-dollar investments:
  * **Nvidia:** **$500 billion** for AI infrastructure and supercomputers.
  * **TSMC:** **$265 billion** for semiconductor manufacturing.
  * **Micron:** **$250 billion** for memory fabrication.
  * **IBM:** Over **$150 billion**.
  * **SpaceX:** **$55 billion**.
  * **Anthropic:** **$50 billion** for AI infrastructure.

## Data Centers & Local Pushback
* **Data Center Narrative:** Secretary Lutnik dismissed local opposition and utility concerns over data centers as misinformation driven by geopolitical adversaries trying to slow U.S. progress.
* **Power and Prosperity:** Lutnik argued that data center operators will build their own power sources—lowering local energy costs rather than raising them—while dramatically expanding the local tax base.
* **Moratorium Warnings:** Communities enacting data center moratoriums (such as Orange County, North Carolina) risk losing economic opportunity to rival regions that roll out the red carpet.

## International Relations & Export Controls
* **China Relations:** President Trump offered to sell H200 Nvidia chips and AMD equivalents to China, but Chinese officials have not taken up the offer due to internal concerns; the administration considers the matter closed.
* **Export Controls & Remote Access:** Secretary Lutnik stated the administration is combating remote-access loopholes using a "whack-a-mole" approach bolstered by AI-driven monitoring of data center usage and token sales.
* **American AI Exports Program:** Led by Secretary Lutnik, the program assists international partners in acquiring U.S. chips, hyperscalers, and models through a "jam-packed" export center.

## AI Models, Safety, and Regulation
* **Frontier vs. Open-Weight Models:** Secretary Lutnik described open-weight models as "distilled" teacher-student models that inherently lag behind continuously advancing frontier models, remaining about two versions behind.
* **Voluntary Review Framework:** Director Katzios explained that an executive order signed in early June allows frontier model developers to voluntarily share models with the U.S. government to harden cybersecurity infrastructure for the government and trusted partners. (Note: Anthropic released Claude 5.1 the day prior.)
* **Defining "Novel Considerations":** Director Katzios cited commercial drone operations under the first Trump administration as an example of a novel situation requiring new FAA airspace rules because existing frameworks were unsuited to the scale of operations.

> "The AI stack is like a five layer cake, right? There's core fundamentals, but there are also opportunities for each country to have their national champions participate in any layer or multiple layers of that cake." — Jensen Huang (cited by Howard Lutnik)

> "These frontier models bring as we discussed today they bring the world's knowledge in a bottle to each economy right and to each community and to each neighborhood." — Howard Lutnik

> "We want more growth and innovation around the world. Innovation that leads to technological progress is how humanity grows the proverbial economic pie." — Michael Katzios

briefings.title: LIVE: OpenAI's Sam Altman speaks at G20 Innovation Ministerial
briefings.tldr: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman argues that AI represents a historic, continuous technological revolution akin to electricity, predicting that making intelligence abundant and inexpensive will fuel an unprecedented boom in global entrepreneurship and education while requiring massive infrastructure investment and proactive risk management.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman argues that AI represents a historic, continuous technological revolution akin to electricity, predicting that making intelligence abundant and inexpensive will fuel an unprecedented boom in global entrepreneurship and education while requiring massive infrastructure investment and proactive risk management.

## Origins and Evolution of OpenAI
* **Early Beginnings:** Sam Altman notes he was a lifelong AI and sci-fi nerd who initially studied the field in school, only to abandon it when "nothing was working" in favor of entrepreneurship. 
* **The Deep Learning Watershed:** In 2012, deep learning emerged as a working paradigm that scaled with compute, prompting Altman and others to launch OpenAI at the very end of 2015 (with work beginning in January 2016).
* **Technological Milestones:** 
  * *Early Focus:* Initial work involved reinforcement learning problems like training a robot hand to solve a Rubik’s cube and playing video games.
  * *Supervised Learning & Scaling:* Progress on supervised learning began around 2018; GPT-1 launched shortly after. 
  * *Usability Threshold:* GPT-3 trained in 2020, representing the first model to cross a threshold of usability where it generated coherent sentences.
  * *The GPT-4 Turning Point:* Internal consensus on the true power of scaling laws solidified around the release of GPT-4 in March 2023, following an eight-month internal testing window.

## The Economic and Entrepreneurial Boom
* **Democratization of Enterprise:** Altman describes AI as "intelligence in a bottle" and "education in a bottle," asserting that it will drive the greatest boom in entrepreneurship and small business creation in history.
* **Real-World Impact:** 
  * *Early Examples:* Cited a laundromat manager who used early iterations of ChatGPT to handle marketing, legal contracts, and vendor relations in 2023.
  * *Agent Evolution:* Coding agents and white-collar work agents accelerated in 2025, paving the way for long-term, persistent virtual collaborators.
  * *Productivity Multiplier:* Startup acceleration work that historically took three months can now be accomplished in approximately 17 minutes using coding tools like CodeX.
* **Global Imperative:** Altman calls AI adoption non-negotiable for G20 economies, comparing refusing to adopt AI to refusing to adopt electricity. He notes that while governments can choose whether to build or rent data centers, embracing the economic growth and medical/educational benefits is vital.

## OpenAI's Strategy and Identity
* **Pragmatic Centrists:** OpenAI positions itself between blind optimism and doomerism, aiming to navigate the transformation's complexity without falling into ideological extremes.
* **Platform and Sovereignty:** OpenAI views itself as a platform provider, intending to respect national sovereignty by letting different countries apply their own context while building in sufficient constraints to prevent catastrophic risks.
* **Pro-Human Stance:** Altman emphasizes that OpenAI is firmly "on team humanity," maintaining that people must remain at the center of the economy, society, and global decision-making.

## Scaling, Infrastructure, and Accessibility
* **Exponential Token Growth:** 
  * *Historical Scale:* At the beginning of 2020, the token leader at OpenAI used roughly 100,000 tokens a month, whereas by mid-2026, leading users process hundreds of billions of tokens per month.
  * *Per Capita Shift:* Global per capita token usage has gone from effectively zero to 100,000 tokens a month.
* **Infrastructure Demand:** Despite algorithmic and hardware efficiency gains (such as manufacturing better chips), massive infrastructure investments will be required to keep intelligence abundant and inexpensive rather than a luxury good.
* **The Light Bulb Analogy:** Altman compares AI's future pricing to the cost of an hour of light at night, which plummeted from five hours of labor to near-zero cost due to energy generation and LED efficiencies; he aims for AI to follow a similar curve of radical democratization.

## Risk Management and Challenges
* **Cybersecurity:** Altman highlights cybersecurity as an urgent, top-of-mind risk where things could go very wrong unless governments and organizations act quickly.
* **Biosecurity:** Biosecurity represents another major hurdle that society must successfully navigate over the next five years.
* **Concentration of Power:** Preventing AI from becoming a scarce, highly contested resource for the rich is essential to avoid worsening global inequality.
* **The Fire Analogy:** Just as human ingenuity made fire safe after early cities burned down through policy and technology, Altman expresses optimism that humanity can successfully mitigate AI downsides through active worry and problem-solving.

## Notable Quotes
> *"If I were a country, ... for sure, I think it is non-negotiable that you have to use it. The economic growth and benefit to people that can come from this. ... the value to a country is too high to ignore."* — Sam Altman

> *"We want to be a reliable partner. ... We really do view what we are doing as a platform as a service to the world. We realize that different people around the world are going to use it very differently and we want to put sufficient constraints on our system to avoid catastrophic risks."* — Sam Altman

> *"I think it would be approximately as bad of an idea to say we're not going to have AI in our country as it was to say we're not going to have electricity in our country, you know, back 100 plus years ago."* — Sam Altman

> *"We are very firmly and very proudly on team humanity. ... We would like people's lives to be better. ... we think that people need to be at the center of the economy and society and global decision-m[aking] and that people should run the future in AI."* — Sam Altman

briefings.title: Sam Altman And Howard Lutnick Discuss AI, Economy At G20 Innovation Ministerial
briefings.tldr: Sam Altman discusses the evolution of OpenAI and artificial intelligence with Howard Lutnick at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, framing AI as an inevitable, electricity-like global commodity that will drive unprecedented economic growth, entrepreneurship, and democratization of education.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sam Altman discusses the evolution of OpenAI and artificial intelligence with Howard Lutnick at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, framing AI as an inevitable, electricity-like global commodity that will drive unprecedented economic growth, entrepreneurship, and democratization of education.

## Origins and Evolution of OpenAI
* **Founding Context:** **Sam Altman** notes he was a sci-fi nerd who studied AI in school before leaving due to lack of progress, returning after the 2012 deep learning watershed moment led him and others to launch OpenAI at the very end of 2015 (first workday January 2016).
* **Early Research Focus:** **Sam Altman** explains that initial work focused on scaling compute to train robot hands for Rubik's cubes and playing video games before unsupervised learning breakthroughs began around 2018.
* **Model Milestones:** **Sam Altman** cites GPT-3 in 2020 as the first model crossing a threshold of usability, followed by GPT-4 in March 2023 (after 8 months of internal testing) as the consensus turning point where internal skeptics realized the technology would go very far.

## AI as an Economic and Entrepreneurial Boom
* **Small Business Catalyst:** **Sam Altman** describes AI as the greatest boom in entrepreneurship and small business creation in history, citing an early 2023 example of a laundromat manager using a broken, early version of ChatGPT to handle marketing, legal contracts, and vendor relationships.
* **Generational Progression:** **Sam Altman** outlines the timeline of agent utility: 
  * *2023:* Early, basic task management and rudimentary assistance.
  * *2025:* Acceleration in coding agents and white-collar work agents.
  * *Near Future:* Long-term persistent agents acting as real virtual collaborators.
* **National Imperative:** **Sam Altman** asserts that for any country, embracing AI is non-negotiable due to massive economic growth, high-value problem solving, and improved individual quality of life in areas like medical care and education.

## Technology as a Continuous Exponential
* **Historical Continuum:** **Sam Altman** rejects viewing AI as an isolated revolution, instead framing it as a single ongoing exponential of technology built on the scaffolding of the agricultural, industrial, and computer revolutions.
* **Context and Sovereignty:** **Sam Altman** emphasizes that OpenAI provides the "engine" or intelligence commodity, while governments, societies, and individuals must supply the necessary context, questions, and ambition to deploy it locally under their own regulatory approaches.
* **The "Pragmatic Centrist" DNA:** **Sam Altman** differentiates OpenAI by striving to avoid blind optimism and doomerism, positioning the company as a reliable platform partner that respects national sovereignty, opposes monopolistic value-sucking, and remains firmly on "team humanity."

## Infrastructure, Abundance, and Token Growth
* **The Scale of Demand:** **Sam Altman** contrasts token usage milestones to illustrate explosive growth:
  * *Early 2020:* The global token leader (an OpenAI employee) used roughly 100,000 tokens a month; average per capita usage was near zero.
  * *Mid-2026:* The top known token user consumes hundreds of billions of tokens a month, while global per capita usage has reached 100,000 tokens a month.
  * *6.5-Year Projection:* Per capita usage is projected to reach 100 billion tokens a month, with top users consuming 100 trillion tokens a month.
* **The Electricity Analogy:** **Sam Altman** compares AI to the dramatic cost reduction of lighting and electricity over time, arguing that massive infrastructure investment and efficiency gains (chips, algorithms) are required to make intelligence an abundant, inexpensive commodity rather than an exclusive luxury.

## Risks, Challenges, and Risk Mitigation
* **Critical Bottlenecks:** **Sam Altman** identifies severe risks over the next five years that could set the technology back, specifically highlighting urgent cyber security vulnerabilities and biosecurity challenges.
* **Equitable Access:** **Sam Altman** warns against the dangerous concentration of power and wealth where rich people compete heavily for scarce compute, stressing that AI must be made abundant to act as an equalizing force rather than worsening inequality.
* **Value of Worry:** **Sam Altman** argues that anxiety and worry are necessary tools for anticipating problems and engineering safety measures—analogous to fire safety innovations preventing city-wide fires—rather than reasons to reject progress.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "In another six and a half years, the average per capita use of tokens will go up to... 100 billion tokens a month. And the person using the most in the world will be using... 100 trillion tokens a month." — **Sam Altman**
* "My prediction is we won't be talking about AI as much as we do in a decade from now because we'll just expect it everywhere." — **Sam Altman**

## Notable Quotes
> "If you have a great idea but you didn't have the resources or the ability to get enough capital together or hire enough experts to work on it or to figure out what it's going to take to invent a new piece of science or manage a complex supply chain. you can do that with AI now." — **Sam Altman**

> "We are the pragmatic centrists. We realize like we want to be we want to be accurate in how we talk about what we see in the future. We don't want to fall into the trap of blind optimism. We don't want to fall into the trap of dumerism." — **Sam Altman**

> "A kid growing up today will never be smarter than AI but he or she will also never have understood a world where every product and service that they interact with is not really smart and really capable and really helpful." — **Sam Altman**
